Subject: SolaceHealth - Data Use Boundaries & BAA Scope

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking the intro with our team last week. As we move toward procurement, our security and legal teams have asked for a concise mapping of how Redwood will handle PHI for the specific integration we discussed (real-time clinical notes ingestion + embeddings).

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirmation that Redwood will be a "service provider" under a standard BAA and whether Redwood will accept a customer-supplied BAA redline.
- Data residency: confirmation that PHI will only be stored in the US and retained per our retention policy (90 days raw, 365 days embeddings).
- Data classification: what is persisted server-side vs. transient in-memory/KV cache?
- Encryption: at-rest and in-transit algorithms and key management (do you support customer-managed keys?).
- Auditability: logs and access controls we can request during onboarding or for audits.

Can you point us to any existing templated contractual language or a short evidence pack? We'll attach our security questionnaire in a follow-up.

Appreciate it — Emily
Emily Zhao
Director, Vendor Risk Management
SolaceHealth

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Rachel (Product Compliance) to respond with specifics; adding Neha from Security for encryption & logging details.

Quick answers while the team compiles a formal packet: 
- BAA: yes, Redwood executes a standard BAA and we are open to limited customer redlines; Laura will propose next steps for review.
- Data residency: hosted deployments in our US region will ensure PHI is stored in US-only zones. We can confirm region and tenancy in the SOW.
- Retention: default retention windows are configurable; we can meet the 90/365 windows you outlined and document that in the data processing addendum.
- Data classification & caching: embeddings are persisted; raw documents can be optionally stored or kept only in KV cache depending on your configuration. Rachel will include a matrix.
- Keys: we support cloud KMS integrations and offer a private deployment path for customer-managed HSMs.

I'll send a proposed action plan and a draft BAA for your legal team to review by EOD Thursday. Suggested next step: 30-minute technical + legal sync next week to walk the questionnaire and the proposed redlines. What time windows look good?

Best,
Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SolaceHealth - Data Use Boundaries & BAA Scope

Hi Emily — Laura here from Legal. Thanks for the questionnaire — we've reviewed it and provided preliminary responses below and attached a draft BAA for redline. Please note these are standard positions; happy to discuss specifics on a call.

1) BAA acceptance and redlines - Redwood executes our standard BAA (attached: redwood_baa_draft_v1.pdf). We will accept customer redlines that do not impose operational requirements inconsistent with our deployment controls (example: changes that require continuous data access for the customer). Please indicate any clauses you anticipate we'll need to revisit and we can pre-scope exceptions.

2) Data residency & retention - Confirmed: production PHI for SolaceHealth will be provisioned in our US region (us-west-2 by default).
- Retention: We will apply a retention policy matching your ask (90-day raw artifacts purge, 365-day embeddings retention). This will be codified in the DPA/SOW.

3) Data classification and storage patterns - See attached 'data_classification_matrix.xlsx'. Summary: raw clinical notes are optional to persist; if persisted they are stored in encrypted object storage with access controls. KV cache used for inference is in-memory with ephemeral encryption and expires per session TTL; we do not rely on cache for long-term persistence. Embeddings are stored and versioned in our embeddings store for indexing and retrieval.

4) Encryption & key management - In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers.
- At-rest: AES-256; object storage and DB encryption.
- KMS: we support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault). For customer-managed keys, we offer a Private deployment option that integrates with your HSM/KMS. Neha, please attach the KMS integration checklist separately.

5) Auditability & logs - We provide request-level audit logs with caller identity, request timestamps, and model run metadata. Logs are retained per contract and can be exported to your SIEM or a secure S3 bucket for audits. We can also provide a redacted SOC 2 attestation and a SOC 2 summary. Link to redacted SOC 2 report below.

Next steps suggested:
- Ben to provide the draft SOW/DPA with retention windows and provisioning region.
- Schedule a 45-minute technical + legal call (we can cover the questionnaire and BAA redline).
- We will upload a zipped evidence pack (SOC 2 summary, SOC 2 redaction, KMS checklist, data matrix) to a secure link by EOD today.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett | Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
